objective: The model-mount MCP `act` tool is a draw-down client: its advertised filters are a read projection of the daemon-resolved standing lease, and editing the host's own filter config changes nothing the daemon enforces.
falsifiable_claim: GET /v1/model-mount/mcp/act/tools renders one act descriptor per connection whose filters (operations, tools, metered unit, usages, budget, expiry) and capability handle come from the connector record's standing lease, with host_config_is_authority=false and an unbounded connection advertised as not actable with its reason; POST /v1/model-mount/mcp/act completes a bounded act without a per-call signature by delegating to the SAME connector-invoke draw-down gate, and a request carrying widened host_filters still refuses at the lease bound while the answer states the host filters were ignored.
adversarial_or_fault_proof: The mutation drill widens the host config's filters beyond the lease (a tool the template does not name, 9999 usages, a 999999-microUSD unit) and requires the daemon to refuse at the lease bound anyway, with host_filters_ignored=true on the answer; the act tool draws the same envelope as every other path, so its third draw exhausts a 3-usage lease and its fourth refuses on max_usages.
remaining_nonclaims: The act tool mints no authority and owns no second gate: it projects the lease and delegates to the connector-invoke draw-down path, so everything it can do is what that gate admits.
The tool is advertised over the daemon's own model-mount route; no agent host's tool registry is modified by this unit, which is the point — a host's registry is a projection.
Provider-side spend (M03.10's provider envelope) is a separate lane; this unit's acts are connector operations.
